decision: A knowledge graph entry must be drafted and presented before any file is written.
why: An entry written without review enters the graph unchallenged, and the graph is what every later change is read against.
steps: Identify whether the entry is new or existing. Read the existing file before drafting an update.
Choose the node type and follow its schema. Constitutive rules define what counts; regulative rules state requirements for entities or processes.
For individual rule files, match the ID to the filename and anchor the rule to a foundation. Constitutive subjects name vocabulary terms; regulative subjects specify entity or process.
For regulative rules, explain what fails without the requirement. Name the constitutive rules upheld in implements, or omit it when serving the foundation directly.
Add dependency links only where the source needs the target. Name the required constraint, fact, or output in the note; omit obvious relationships.
Present the complete draft and wait for permission to write.
Write the approved entry and regenerate constitution/graph.md with .github/scripts/write-knowledge-graph.ps1.
violations: File written before a draft was presented.
Link added in both directions between two entries.
Violation that restates the rule instead of describing a detectable breach.
A decision field combining two different concerns into one rule.
